solves: Groups on one surface the content and the actions of one subject, for the person to read, compare or open that subject: the summary of a record, an item of a collection or a block of data on a detail page.
use_when: A subject stands on its own and has its own actions, such as open or approve: the base type, choosing between actions inside the card or the whole card clickable.
An item of a collection leads to another page and holds nothing interactive inside: the clickable type.
A block of data of a detail page, with one action such as edit in the header: the section type.
The card sits on the page background: the elevated surface. The card sits inside another surface or in a dense list: the outlined surface.
A dense list or a narrow panel: the compact density; the default density elsewhere.
The image identifies the item: media at the top. The text is the main thing and the image supports it: media at the side.
The start says what the card is: an icon for the kind of subject, an avatar for a person, an image for an object or a file.
The footer has actions: keep the divider before them. The meta footer of the clickable card has no divider.
do_not_use_when: For items in sequence with no container of their own: use a list.
For comparing data in columns: use nph-table.
To choose one among several: use nph-rich-option, which is the selectable card.
For content that opens and closes: use nph-collapsible, which is the expandable card.
For a layer that floats over the page: use nph-popover, nph-hover-card or nph-dialog.
For a collection or a gallery: the layout is the product's, a list or a grid of cards.
Inside another card: a card never holds a card.

type.constraint: The Figma property `tipo`. base is a card with its own content and actions; it takes no focus and has no role. clickable is a card whose whole area leads to a destination through the link on its title, with the arrow and a meta footer; it has no header action, no tonal section and no divider. section is a block of data of a detail page, a region named by its title, with the key-value list of items and, when on, a header action with text. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the box by it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

surface.constraint: The Figma property `superfície`. elevated has the soft outline and the raised shadow; in dark the shadow goes away and the background above the page separates it with the outline. outlined has the same outline and no shadow. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the shadow by it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

media.constraint: The Figma property `mídia`. It needs one piece in the media slot, an nph-image. top is the card width in 16:9, clipped by the card corner. inset-top sits inside the body padding with the corner of the large image. side sits at the start, the card height and about 40 percent of the card width, 33 percent in the compact density, with a cover crop; when the card is narrower than 30rem it moves to the top. For the base and clickable types only: in the section type it is ignored and warned once in development. The media box is drawn whenever the value is not none, so a card with no piece in the slot leaves an empty box. A piece in the slot while the value is none, or while the type is section, is not drawn and is warned once. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the box by it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

density.constraint: The Figma property `densidade`. default pads the body by card/padding, with the title in text/heading-md. compact pads it by card/padding-compact, with the title in text/heading-xs, for a dense list and a narrow panel. The start follows the density: the tonal box and the avatar, and the image of the start, take the compact size. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the box by it. A value outside the list draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

disabled.constraint: The clickable type only. The title is drawn with no href, with role link and aria-disabled true, outside the Tab order, the whole card under card/disabled-opacity and with no hover. A disabled card needs no href. In the base and section types it is ignored and warned once in development. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the look by it.

loading.constraint: Any type. The surface, its outline and its padding stay; the content becomes nph-skeleton pieces hidden from assistive technology, aria-busy is true and the hidden word of loading-label is written outside the hidden node. The title, the description, the start, the media, the status, the action, the content and the footer are not drawn; no heading is required. The base and section types keep the divider, unless hide-divider is set, and one action skeleton; the clickable type has no footer and is not a link while it loads. Reflects because the internal CSS selects the look by it.

heading.constraint: The title of the card, already localized, one line with an ellipsis when it does not fit; it truncates before the status, which never hides. It is the accessible name of the clickable card and of the section region. A card that is not loading and has no heading draws nothing and emits console.error in development; while it loads the heading is not required. In the clickable type write the destination, not a generic word.

heading-level.constraint: The level of the title, which is drawn as role heading with aria-level, so a collection of cards keeps the outline of the page. The property is headingLevel. A value outside the list, or a text that is not a number, draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

description.constraint: The short text below the title, already localized, in card/description-foreground. Empty draws none; the part is on when there is text.

icon.constraint: The start icon, a core name of nph-icon in the light weight, drawn in the tonal box and chosen by the kind of subject. Empty draws none. The start takes one piece at a time: with content in the leading slot the icon is ignored and warned once in development. A name outside the core draws nothing and emits console.error in development.

href.constraint: The destination of the title link, for the clickable type; required there unless the card is disabled or loading. It takes http, https, mailto, tel or a relative address; any other protocol, javascript among them, in any spelling the browser reads as such, draws nothing and emits console.error in development, as does a clickable card with none. In the base and section types it is ignored and warned once in development.

loading-label.constraint: The word the screen reader hears while the card loads, already localized, such as Loading. The piece writes no word of its own. Empty with loading on warns once in development: the screen reader hears nothing. The property is loadingLabel.

hide-divider.constraint: The Figma boolean `divisória` is on by default, so the property turns it off. The divider is the nph-separator before the footer actions, edge to edge, in card/divider, and it is drawn when the footer has content. It has no effect on the clickable card, which has no divider, and says so once in development. The property is hideDivider.

items.constraint: Property only. The key-value list of the section type, as a list of { key, value }, both texts already localized. key is required and not empty; value is a text and may be empty. It is drawn as a description list after the default slot, rows card/list-gap apart, the key at the start of the row and the value at its end; a long key or value wraps inside the row. In the base and clickable types a list with rows is ignored and warned once in development. A value that is not a list of rows with a key and a text value draws nothing, in any type, and emits console.error in development.

slot-media.constraint: The media zone: one nph-image with src and alt only. The card gives the frame, the width, the proportion and the crop, whatever size the image declares. It is not the start. Drawn only while media is top, inset-top or side, and not in the section type.

slot-leading.constraint: The start zone, in place of the icon: one nph-avatar or one nph-image. The card writes the size of the density on it: the avatar large, or medium when compact, and the image medium, or small when compact, and writes it again if the piece changes its own. A piece of another tag is left as it is. It is decorative, aria-hidden, in the clickable card.

slot-status.constraint: The status zone: one nph-badge, secondary and light, next to the title. The part is on when there is something in the slot. The title truncates before it.

slot-action.constraint: The header action, the last piece of the header. In the base type, the menu action: an icon-only nph-button, ghost and compact, with the ellipsis-vertical icon and a label that carries the card, such as More options for Order 1042; on a touch screen it is raised to control/height-default. In the section type, an nph-button secondary solid compact with text. Not drawn in the clickable card, which shows the arrow in its place: the slot is dropped and warned once in development.

slot.constraint: The content zone, free: text, fields, metrics or other Nephos pieces, in text/body-md. Never a card inside a card. In the clickable card nothing interactive goes in it, and the card does not police that.

slot-section.constraint: The tonal section: a band in card/section-background with the label and the text of one highlighted passage, no border and no shadow. Not drawn in the clickable card: the slot is dropped and warned once in development.

slot-footer.constraint: The footer zone. In the base and section types, the nph-button actions aligned to the end, secondary solid before primary solid, card/footer-gap apart, after the divider. In the clickable card, a meta text in the body, aligned to the start in card/description-foreground, with no divider.

type.choose_when: base for a subject with its own actions; clickable when the whole card leads to another page and nothing interactive sits inside; section for a block of data of a detail page, with a key-value list.
do_not_combine_with: header action, tonal section, divider or buttons with clickable

surface.choose_when: elevated on the page background; outlined inside another surface or in a dense list. The cards of a grid share one surface.

media.choose_when: top when the image identifies the item; inset-top when the image sits inside the padding; side when the text is the main thing and the image supports it, in a card wider than 30rem.

density.choose_when: compact in a dense list or a narrow panel; default elsewhere. The cards of a grid share one density.

default.token: card/background, card/foreground, card/description-foreground, card/border, card/border-width, card/radius, elevation/raised
default.changes_for_user: The soft outline on both surfaces; the raised shadow on the elevated one only. The clickable card always shows the arrow in card/indicator-foreground and the meta footer.

hover.changes_for_user: The clickable card only: the outline color rises. The background and the shadow stay, the width does not change, nothing animates, and the hover does not move the focus. The base and section cards have no hover.

focus.token: focus/border, border/width, focus/border-radius-surface, focus/halo, focus/ring-width, focus/radius-surface-with-border
focus.changes_for_user: The clickable card only, for keyboard users: a border and, beyond it, a halo around the whole card, outside it. A pointer press draws none. The base card takes no focus; the controls inside it keep their own.

disabled.changes_for_user: The clickable card only: the whole card is faded, is not a link and leaves the Tab order. Disabled wins over hover and focus.

loading.token: card/header-gap, card/gap, card/footer-padding, card/footer-padding-compact, the tokens of nph-skeleton
loading.changes_for_user: The surface, its outline and its padding stay and skeleton pieces take the place of the content, hidden from assistive technology; aria-busy is true and the screen reader hears the loading word.

business_rules: The card is a surface for one subject. Besides the container only the title is required; every other zone turns on and off.

The parts that turn on and off come from the content, never from a boolean property: the start is on with an icon or a piece in the leading slot, the description with text, the status, action, section and footer with something in their slot, the content with something in the default slot or rows in items. The divider is on when the footer is, unless hide-divider is set, and the clickable card has none. Only the divider has a property, because it is on by default.
Hover only changes the outline color and the width never changes, so the card does not move between states.
The clickable card is a native link: the title, inside the heading, is the only Tab stop and the link area is stretched over the whole card with CSS only. Enter opens it and Space does nothing.
Nothing interactive goes inside the clickable card: no header action, no tonal section, no divider and no buttons; the start and the arrow are decorative.
The card draws a focus look only on the clickable type. The controls inside a base or section card keep their own focus.
The section type is a region named by its title. The base card has no role and is not a landmark; a collection is the consumer's list, one li per card.
While loading no real content is drawn, the title included, and the card names itself by aria-busy and the hidden word, which the consumer gives already localized.
The side media moves to the top when the card is narrower than 30rem. The card takes the width of its container and needs one: it fills a block, and in a flex row it needs a basis.

Touch: the menu action of the base card is raised from control/height-compact to control/height-default under a coarse pointer, by writing the compact height on the slotted action from outside. The text button of the section type keeps its size.

The card changes none of the pieces it draws or places. What it sets on them it sets from outside: the separator line, the arrow color, the sizes of an icon, the frame of the media, the size of the start avatar and image, and the height of the menu action on touch.
Every text comes from the consumer, already localized: the card writes no word of its own.
There is no transition and no animation, so there is nothing to reduce under reduced motion.
domain_errors: A type, surface, media, density or heading-level outside its list, or an icon that is not a core name of nph-icon: the card draws nothing and emits console.error in development, once per cause.
A card that is not loading with no heading: it draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
A clickable card, not disabled and not loading, with no href or with an unsafe one: it draws nothing and emits console.error in development.
An items value that is not a list of rows with a non-empty key and a text value: it draws nothing, in any type, and emits console.error in development.

An href or a disabled outside the clickable type, a media in the section type, items outside the section type, an action or a section slot in the clickable card, hide-divider on the clickable card, an icon next to a leading piece, a piece in the media slot with no media: the card ignores it and emits console.warn in development, once per cause.
Loading with no loading-label: the card draws and warns once in development that the screen reader hears nothing.

tokens.surface: card/background, card/foreground, card/border, card/border-width, card/radius, elevation/raised
tokens.start: card/icon-container-background, card/icon-container-foreground, card/icon-container-radius, card/icon-container-padding, card/icon-size, card/icon-size-dense
tokens.focus: focus/border, border/width, focus/border-radius-surface, focus/halo, focus/ring-width, focus/radius-surface-with-border

ai_hints: Use nph-card for one subject that stands on its own; for items in sequence use a list, for comparing columns use nph-table, to choose one use nph-rich-option, and for content that opens and closes use nph-collapsible.
Always give heading, already localized; it is the only required zone. In the clickable type write the destination in it, because the name read is the title.
Choose the type by what the card does: base for its own actions, clickable when the whole card leads to a page, section for a block of data with a key-value list.
For the clickable type give href and nothing interactive: no action, no section, no buttons, no divider. Put the meta text in the footer slot.
Fill a zone by its slot name and leave the others empty: media, leading, status, action, section and footer, with the content in the default slot. Do not look for a boolean property per part.
Give the key-value list of the section type through items as a property, a list of key and value, never as slotted markup.
Slot one nph-image with src and alt only in the media slot; the card gives the frame. Slot an nph-avatar or an nph-image in leading, or set icon, never both.

Put the menu action in the action slot of the base card as an icon-only nph-button, ghost and compact, with a label such as More options for plus the title; use an nph-button secondary solid compact with text in the section type.
Put at most one primary action in the footer, after the secondary one; never a destructive action in the header action.
Set heading-level so the title fits the outline of the page, 3 by default, and wrap a collection in a ul with one li per card and a name on the list.
Set loading with loading-label, already localized; give no heading and no content while it loads.
Use one surface and one density across the cards of a grid; use outlined inside another surface or in a dense list, compact in a narrow panel.
Give the card a container width: it fills a block, and in a flex row it needs a basis.

accessibility.semantics: There is no card pattern in the WAI-ARIA APG. The title is a div with role heading and aria-level, set by heading-level. The clickable card is the link pattern: the title text is an a inside the heading, stretched over the card with CSS only; the disabled one is an a with role link and aria-disabled true and no href, and the inner surface box of a disabled clickable card carries aria-disabled true too. The base card has no role and takes no focus. The section card is a region named by the title through aria-labelledby, or by aria-label from the heading while loading, and has no role while loading with no heading. The key-value list is a description list. The start and the arrow of the clickable card are aria-hidden. Loading sets aria-busy true on the surface and the skeleton is aria-hidden, with the hidden word outside the hidden node.
accessibility.accessible_name: The clickable card is named by its title, the text of the link. The section card is named by its title. The base card has no name of its own; the icon-only menu action carries a label with the verb and the card title, such as More options for Order 1042. A collection is a ul with a name on the list.
keyboard: Tab on the base card stops only on the controls inside it, the menu action and the footer buttons; the card itself takes no focus.
Tab on the clickable card has one stop, the title link; it has no control inside.
Enter on the clickable card opens the link. Space does nothing: it is a link, not a button.
Tab on the section card stops only on the controls inside it, the header action and the footer buttons.
A disabled clickable card leaves the Tab order.
The menu action follows the APG menu button: Enter, Space or Down Arrow open the menu and focus the first item, Up Arrow focuses the last, and Escape closes it and returns the focus to the action.
accessibility.focus: The clickable card only, for keyboard users only: on the link focus-visible, a border in focus/border and, beyond it, a halo in focus/halo, around the whole card, outside it, with their own corners. The card never clips, so the look is not cut. A pointer press draws none. The hover does not move the focus. With forced colors the outline is a system color and the focus is another.
accessibility.contrast: The title in card/foreground and the description in card/description-foreground pass 4.5:1 over the card in both themes, also over the tonal section. The start icon in card/icon-container-foreground passes 3:1 over its box in every brand and both themes, 4.64:1 or more. The focus border is measured over color/background: 5.37:1 in light in the default brand, 4.32:1 or more in every brand, and 11.7:1 in dark in the default brand; its measure against the halo, the neighbor outside the border, is pending, and the known limit of focus/border in the light `Sistemas` brand applies. The halo is a reinforcement. The soft outline over the card is about 1.1:1 in light and 1.35:1 in dark and is decorative: the background and the shadow separate the card from the page. The hover outline is 1.69:1 to 3.53:1 and needs no 3:1, because the pointer is the cue. The start box over the card is 1.04:1 to 1.25:1 in dark, decorative, and the icon carries the cue. A disabled card is outside the contrast requirement.
accessibility.color_alternative: The clickable card shows the arrow and the meta text, not only the hover outline. The status carries text in the badge, not only color. Loading is told by the skeleton and the hidden word, and disabled by the opacity and by leaving the Tab order.

invalid_combinations: A type, surface, media, density or heading-level outside its list, or an icon that is not a core name — the card draws nothing.
A card that is not loading with no heading — the card draws nothing.
A clickable card with no href or an unsafe one, when it is not disabled and not loading — the card draws nothing.
A malformed items, in any type — the card draws nothing.
A header action, a tonal section, a divider or hide-divider with the clickable type — the slots are dropped and hide-divider has no effect, with a warning.
Interactive content in the default, status or footer slot of the clickable card — a link inside a link; the card does not police it.
An href or a disabled with the base or section type — ignored with a warning.
A media in the section type, or a piece in the media slot with media none — not drawn, with a warning.
Items with the base or clickable type — ignored with a warning.
An icon with a piece in the leading slot — the icon is ignored with a warning; the start takes one piece at a time.
A card inside a card, two primary actions in the footer, or a destructive action in the header action.

combines_with: nph-icon-button, an nph-button with no text
parents: a page, a panel, a grid or a list: the container gives the width
an li of a ul, for a collection of cards
children: nph-icon, nph-separator and nph-skeleton, drawn by the card
nph-image, nph-avatar, nph-badge, nph-button, slotted by the consumer, the icon-only one included
free content in the default slot
appears_in: a summary of a record with actions, in the base type
a navigable collection, in the clickable type with media at the top
a detail block in a panel, in the section type, outlined
a profile, with an avatar at the start
a file, with a thumbnail at the start and the menu action

anti_patterns: Putting two primary actions in the footer: use one primary solid and the others secondary solid.
Putting a destructive action in the header action: use a button with text in the footer.
Using a generic title on the clickable card: write the destination, because the name read is the title.
Putting a button, a link or a menu inside the clickable card, or a header action, a tonal section or a divider.
Putting a divider between the parts of the body: the card separates by space and the only divider is the one before the footer actions.
Putting a card inside another card.
Mixing surfaces or densities among the cards of a grid: a difference looks like hierarchy.
Using the card for selection, which is nph-rich-option, or for content that opens and closes, which is nph-collapsible.
Setting a size on the slotted nph-image to frame the media, or writing the size of the start avatar or image: the card does that.
Slotting an icon next to a leading piece, or an empty piece in the media slot.
Putting the loading word, the title or the list as slotted markup instead of loading-label, heading and items.
Relying on the card for the collection list: the ul and the li are the consumer's.
